reason: Attacked on five fronts and it held on all five. (1) WORDING, including the leading Yet, which was the obvious place to break it: three independent transcriptions give the sentence identically, and one of them settles the Yet by printing what comes before it. Stephen Sparks’s in-order passage list has the sentence inside the same paragraph as its antecedent: “The talking tribe, I find, want sensation from the mountain ... They want the startling view, the horrid pinnacle ... Yet often the mountain gives itself most completely when I have no destination, when I reach nowhere in particular, but have gone out merely to be with the mountain as one visits a friend with no intention but to be with him.” The Yet is adversative to the talking tribe and is the text’s own word, not a splice; stripping it, which is how many aggregators print the line, would be the error. No comma after “friend” in any of the three. (2) TRANSLATION DRIFT, this track’s usual killer, cannot arise: Shepherd wrote in English and the line names no translator. (3) LOCATOR. The readingandwalking.ca reader is explicitly working from the Canongate 2011 paperback with Macfarlane’s introduction and walks the second chapter page by page, quoting at (9), (10), (11), (13), (14), then this sentence at (15), then opening the next paragraph “The third chapter, ‘The Group’ ...” at (16). That is a demonstrated chapter boundary, not an assertion: p. 15 is the last page of chapter 2, The Recesses. A second source independently cites it as (Shepherd 2011: 15). The curator’s own locator detail, that it falls a few lines after the horrid-pinnacle sentence, is corroborated from the other direction by the same reader’s summary that listening in the hills beats speaking. (4) ATTRIBUTION. Shepherd’s own first-person prose, so there is no speaker to name and no reporter trap; the line is on none of the brief’s misattribution rows. (5) SCOPE AND FORM. First published 1977, Aberdeen University Press, so pre-1999; prose nonfiction, and Essay is the right tag in the closed vocabulary; publishable; on the theme of the Way. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Shepherd 0 of 3 in the year, not banned, not in personsUsed. Source line leads with the name, 105 characters, no dash (a semicolon carries the first-published note), no straight double quote; the quotation is unbroken prose ending in a full stop. ONE HONEST LIMIT, which the verifier already stated rather than hid: the printed page was not seen. I tried and could not open it either. Both archive.org copies are lending-restricted: livingmountaince0000shep (Canongate 2011) and bwb_KR-674-517 (the 1984 Aberdeen printing) both return 401 on the djvu text and “Item not available” on search-inside. That matters for one claim in the CURATOR’s locator, which says the line was “read in the archive.org scan of the 1984 Aberdeen printing (bwb_KR-674-517)”; that reading is not reproducible and should not be relied on. The verifier was right to drop it and to say the page was not seen. The citation stands on three independent witnesses to the wording and a page-by-page reader of the named edition, which is what this standard asks for, so I leave betterCitation empty.
